content.title: Patriots’ Day 2026: Concord brings history to life as US celebrates 250 years of independence
content.text: History buffs, proud New Englanders, early birds and tourists bore witness to history Sunday as Colonial Militia gathered in the pre-dawn light on Buttrick Hillside and Old Manse Hill in Minute Man National Historic Park.The battle at Old North Bridge — often referred to as the spot where the “shot heard ‘round the world” launched the revolution — happened on April 19, 1775.Last year marked that battle’s 250th anniversary, to much fanfare. This year, the country celebrates the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence.What happened in Concord in 1775?According to the National Park Service: “On the morning of April 19, 1775, Colonial Militia from Concord and surrounding towns exchanged gunfire with British regulars guarding the critical river crossing. Although the fighting at the North Bridge lasted only a few seconds, it marked the beginning of a massive battle that raged over 16 miles along the Bay Road from Boston to Concord, and included some 1,700 British regulars and over 4,000 Colonial militia.”Reenactors gathered in the pre-dawn light of Sunday at the Minuteman National Historic Park to recreate the events that happened on this land 251 years ago.(Sebastian Restrepo/MassLive)Sunday kicked off with a dawn salute, with reenactors mustering at Buttrick Hillside at 5:45 a.m., followed by bells tolling as an alarm from First Parish at 6 a.m. “‘Dr. Prescott’ arrives at the North Bridge after riding across the fields calling out the warning to towns and villages that the Regulars were on the march and that their destination was Concord,” the Concord250 website explained. “The Concord Minutemen fire salutes and the Concord Independent Battery fire several volleys from the field at the Old Manse.”“Two hundred fifty years ago, the people of what is now Massachusetts took a stand for liberty, equality, civil rights, and responsible citizenship,” the site read.Find more historical events happening in Concord here.What about Lexington?Tens of thousands of people also flock to the Lexington Battle Green each year to watch the reenactment of the skirmish that helped launch the Revolutionary War. This year’s reenactment of the battle that left eight Patriots dead and 10 wounded so many years ago was held Saturday.“Lexington was preparing for battle long before British soldiers arrived on April 19th, 1775,” according to the Lex250 website. “Paul Revere and William Dawes, fellow Sons of Liberty, rode hard from Boston, arriving in town just before midnight. Their destination: The home of Reverend Jonas Clarke, cousin to patriot leader John Hancock. Their mission: To warn Patriot leaders John Hancock and Samuel Adams of the impending British raid.”Find more 250th events being celebrated this year in Lexington here and throughout the state here.
